assessment.finding: Own data descriptors snapshot bounded dense canonical Fr arrays and mandatory callback before first await. Protocol-derived 24575-field/6142-transaction bounds, minimum progress, all category maxima, declared total and private/public/class lengths are checked before TxEffect expansion. Footer must be exactly the last seven fields; each must equal reconstructed header end data. No full Body expansion or cross-transaction Promise.all.

Round-trip header fields reject narrowing; supplied expected hash equals actual SDK header hash. Complete ordered effects are decoded and re-encoded exactly, hashed through official category/leaf functions and official ordered unbalanced-tree algorithm, then compared to authenticated header.txEffectsTreeRoot. Empty and single-leaf semantics agree with Body.computeTxEffectsTree. This is full-root reconstruction, not acceptance of an attacker-provided leaf or inclusion path.

Descriptors stay local until every effect/root and the final captured canonical callback succeed. Frozen detached strings/arrays/result and WeakSet brand prevent mutation or copied-brand claims. Errors are collapsed to fixed code/message without foreign cause. Function owns no retry, transport, persistence, queue, node or lifecycle. One expanded effect at a time is a control-flow property; actual garbage-collection/RSS bound remains unmeasured.

Canonical authority is expressly delegated to a trusted caller capability, not inferred from the brand. The callback must independently bind network/version, selected tier, block number/hash and account/lease context. A callback returning true without authenticated chain checks only validates internal consistency. A result can become stale after return; future storage/use needs its own canonical/lease checks.

Returned fields are authenticated public ciphertext descriptors only. No decrypted-note/event authenticity, recipient scope, nullifier processing, encrypted preference head completeness or cold PXE recovery is established. Existing official private-processing semantics must remain authoritative in later integration.
